policies.title: Configuration utility (TMUI) is open to every address
policies.description: Checks that the httpd allow list is not all or a world-wide range.
policies.rationale: The management web interface is a recurring target of authentication-bypass and remote-code-execution advisories; it should only be reachable from management hosts.
policies.absence_note: The setting is not in the submitted file. It may live in another file (bigip_base.conf versus bigip.conf) or rely on a version default that this file cannot show. The default allow list is version specific and was not verified here.
policies.remediation: Restrict sys httpd allow to named management addresses or the management network.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)
F5 K-articles on hardening and port lockdown (named by that article; not opened)

policies.title: SSH is open to every address
policies.description: Checks that the sshd allow list is not all or a world-wide range.
policies.rationale: SSH on the appliance should be limited to management hosts.
policies.absence_note: The setting is not in the submitted file. It may live in another file (bigip_base.conf versus bigip.conf) or rely on a version default that this file cannot show.
policies.remediation: Restrict sys sshd allow to named management addresses.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)

policies.title: Management web interface accepts legacy TLS protocols
policies.description: Checks that the httpd SSL protocol string excludes TLS 1.0 and 1.1 (an explicit modern list, or all with those removed).
policies.rationale: Legacy protocol versions have known weaknesses and are removed from current baselines.
policies.absence_note: The setting is not in the submitted file. It may live in another file (bigip_base.conf versus bigip.conf) or rely on a version default that this file cannot show. The default protocol set differs by version.
policies.remediation: Set the httpd ssl-protocol to TLSv1.2 and above only.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)
F5 K-articles on hardening and port lockdown (named by that article; not opened)

policies.title: Self IP accepts every service
policies.description: Flags self IPs with allow-service all.
policies.rationale: Port lockdown set to allow all exposes control-plane services (SSH, management web) on a data-plane address.
policies.absence_note: No self IP with allow-service all in the submitted file.
policies.remediation: Use allow-service none, or list only the required service ports.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)
F5 K-articles on hardening and port lockdown (named by that article; not opened)

policies.title: Self IP uses the default service allow list
policies.description: Flags self IPs with allow-service default.
policies.rationale: The default list opens several service ports; an explicit short list is easier to review.
policies.absence_note: No self IP with allow-service default in the submitted file.
policies.remediation: Replace default with an explicit list of required ports.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)
F5 K-articles on hardening and port lockdown (named by that article; not opened)

policies.title: SSL profile allows weak ciphers
policies.description: Flags client-ssl and server-ssl profiles whose cipher string names RC4, DES/3DES, MD5, EXPORT, NULL or LOW.
policies.rationale: Weak cipher suites can be broken or downgraded.
policies.absence_note: No SSL profile with an obviously weak cipher string was found.
policies.remediation: Use a cipher string limited to modern AEAD suites.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)
F5 K-articles on hardening and port lockdown (named by that article; not opened)

policies.title: Virtual server listens on every port
policies.description: Flags virtual servers with a wildcard destination port, no source restriction and a set IP protocol.
policies.rationale: A catch-all listener widens the attack surface beyond the intended service.
policies.remediation: Bind the virtual server to the specific service port and restrict the source.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)
F5 K-articles on hardening and port lockdown (named by that article; not opened)

policies.title: SNMP uses a default community string
policies.description: Flags the community names public and private.
policies.rationale: Default community strings are guessed first.
policies.remediation: Use SNMPv3, or a long random community restricted to monitoring hosts.
references: F5 community: Security best practices for BIG-IP and BIG-IQ systems (public)

policies.title: No remote syslog destination configured
policies.description: Checks that the system logs to at least one remote server.
policies.rationale: Off-box logs survive tampering with the appliance and feed detection.
policies.absence_note: No remote-servers entry in the submitted file; it may be in another file.
policies.remediation: Configure a remote syslog server in sys syslog.

policies.title: SSH sessions never time out
policies.description: Checks that the sshd inactivity timeout is greater than zero.
policies.rationale: Idle shells left open are a standing foothold.
policies.absence_note: The setting is not in the submitted file. It may live in another file (bigip_base.conf versus bigip.conf) or rely on a version default that this file cannot show.
policies.remediation: Set inactivity-timeout to a few minutes.
